text:
EDM visits UTA tonight, two days after UTA won the first meeting 4-2, a game the Mammoth deserved to win 65% of the time. The model projects a close one, UTA 3.13 expected goals to EDM's 2.96. UTA has the better chance profile at five on five, with 58% of the expected goals against 52% for EDM, and creates 3.63 expected goals per 60 to the Oilers' 2.96. EDM's results are ahead of its chances: a +9 goal difference on +3.5 expected, with finishing (+10.2 goals against the chances) doing the lifting. Special teams are nearly even, with both penalty kills allowing 0.52 expected goals a game. UTA takes 4.8 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays.

Both teams are 4-1-0 in their last five. UTA took 59% of the expected goals in that stretch and EDM 53%, and the Mammoth have won three straight. In net, Tristan Jarry is projected for EDM, starting over Devon Levi, and he sits at -3.75 goals saved above expected this season (-4.19 last year). Karel Vejmelka is projected for UTA at +1.48 this season and +5.39 last season, a clear edge for the home side.

For EDM, Connor McDavid is on a seven-game point streak and has an 82% chance of a point, and Evan Bouchard has 15 points in his last seven, though finishing is doing most of that work. Zach Hyman could return. For UTA, Dylan Guenther and Nick Schmaltz each have a 32% chance to score.
